overall_summary: Space-themed content featuring extreme physical paradoxes and sensory anomalies (e.g., burning ice, smelling space, molten iron rain) vastly outperforms standard biology, psychology, and cognitive science topics. Additionally, re-uploading identical concepts within short windows yields diminishing algorithmic returns.

winning_patterns.evidence: 'The Planet of Burning Ice Will Break Your Brain!' achieved 1,053 views, 'The Largest Ocean in Space' reached 460 views, and 'What Does Outer Space Actually Smell Like?' secured 368 views.
winning_patterns.action: Double down on space anomalies that challenge common sense, focusing on extreme weather, unexpected smells, or impossible chemistry.

winning_patterns.evidence: 'Sharks Are Older Than Trees?' reached 302 views, showing strong engagement for historical/biological timeline comparisons.
winning_patterns.action: Create content comparing the lifespans of species or ancient structures to modern concepts to trigger cognitive dissonance.

weak_patterns.evidence: 'Your Brain Is Hiding This From You' (38 views) and 'The Real Reason Songs Get Stuck In Your Head' (17 views) consistently underperformed.
weak_patterns.action: Pivot away from abstract internal psychology and focus on external, highly visual cosmic or natural mysteries.

weak_patterns.evidence: 'Your Brain Can Create Fake Memories' got 5 views on Sep 4 and only 52 views when re-uploaded on Sep 7. 'Why Space Is Completely Silent' dropped from 205 views to 61 views on its second posting.
weak_patterns.action: Avoid posting identical scripts or highly similar titles within a 7-day window to prevent algorithmic suppression.
